operations.label: MatMul
operations.note: Native field arithmetic: multiply-accumulate maps directly to constraints (~2 multiplications + additions per output element). This is what ZK circuits do cheaply — no transcendental functions, no lookup benefit.

operations.label: Softmax
operations.note: exp(x)/Σexp has no polynomial form over finite fields. Piecewise polynomial approximation requires 200–350 constraints/element. With LogUp/Lasso, a pre-committed exp() table reduces this to ~20–40 constraints — a 7–14× saving per element.

operations.label: LayerNorm
operations.note: Requires 1/√σ (inverse square root) — non-native in finite fields. Newton–Raphson polynomial approximation costs 100–200 constraints/element. Lookup-based range checks bring this to ~15–25 constraints, a ~7× reduction.

operations.label: GELU / SiLU
operations.note: GELU uses erf(); SiLU uses sigmoid() — both transcendental. In-circuit polynomial approximation is the single most expensive operation: 300–500 constraints/element. Lasso sublinear lookups reduce this to 30–50 constraints, a ~10× saving.

operations.label: Other
operations.note: Residual connections, bias additions, and element-wise additions are native field additions — one gate each. Lookup arguments provide only marginal savings from amortized range checks.
